item.title: UK Advertising Standards Agency Is Looking to Regulate Bogus Mobile Game Adverts
item.description:
Help this bankrupt mother build a roof and eat a baby.

The UK's Advertising Standards Agency (ASA) has made moves to ban online mobile game adverts that wholly misrepresent downloadable games, their contents, and their plaudits. The regulatory body made the ruling following a complaint partly upheld against mobile gaming juggernaut, King.

The ASA successfully banned a Facebook ad for the mobile game Farm Heroes Saga that showed a farmyard-based Match-3 title with graphics, models and special effects that don't appear in the game itself. Despite the advert's use of the modern marketing Get-Out-of-Jail-Free card - the "Not Actual Gameplay" disclaimer - the ASA ruled the ad misleading and ordered its removal from online spaces.

item.title: 'PlayStation: The First 30 Years' Is a Lush Visual History Releasing at a Volatile Time for the Console's Legacy
item.description:
Retrospective available as a Physical Book.

It's a helluva month for PlayStation to release a tome celebrating its 30-year legacy. And, like it or not, it has been an undeniable and indelible three decades for the first-time console maker. Sony stepped into the market in 1996 and not only took on the veterans at their own game, but beat them. Soundly.

PlayStation redefined the entire industry. It brought gaming to the biggest audience it had ever had to that point. It took gaming mainstream, made it "cool" for celebrities to endorse what had then been tediously dubbed a "nerd" pastime, and, from the PS1's launch onwards, PlayStation continued to grow as a globally recognised brand, synonymous with gaming and often considered the flagship platform for all of the industry's biggest releases.

item.title: 'I Don't Think You Can Look at Breath of the Wild and Not See a Little Bit of Deus Ex in It'
item.description:
Warren Spector reflects on his immersive sim legacy.

Warren Spector recently announced his retirement from video game development after a glittering career that includes titles such as Wing Commander, Ultima Underworld: The Stygian Abyss, System Shock, Deus Ex, Thief: Deadly Shadows and Epic Mickey.

One of the genres Spector is most readily associated with is the 'immersive sim' – games populated by real-world mechanics where the player is capable of finding emergent solutions to problems – and titles like Deus Ex and System Shock are seen as seminal entries in this subset of adventure games.

item.title: 'Battlespire Rules' - After 29 Years, the Secret of This Elder Scrolls Easter Egg Has Finally Been Revealed
item.description:
All thanks to the 'Julian LeFay Papers'.

The mysteries of a 29-year old Easter Egg in An Elder Scrolls Legend: Battlespire have finally been solved, due to a new donation to the Strong Museum of Play in Rochester, New York.

Andrew Borman, the director of Digital Preservation at the Strong Museum, took to social media earlier this week to share the exciting news in a short video, documenting the discovery.

item.title: Crazy Taxi Meets GTA In 'Downtown Dash', A New Arcade-Style Racing Game For Your Atari Jaguar
item.description:
Made the "traditional way".

A new 3D racing game has just launched for the Atari Jaguar, combining the open-world chaos and classic camera angles of Grand Theft Auto with the frantic, timer-based mayhem of Crazy Taxi.

Downtown Dash was developed in six months for the JagJam 2026 event and is proudly made "100% without AI" (a refreshing change of pace, considering the state of our news tips over recent months). It is the work of Dr Ludos and was described to us as being developed the "traditional way", with the creator relying on advice, tools, and assets from various members of the Atari Jaguar & retro homebrew communities in order to bring the project to life (as opposed to simply turning to generative AI).

item.title: Former Sega Dev Shares Mega Drive Archive, Inc. Abandoned Code for Segapede, Jester & a Game starring Sonic's Pal, Tails
item.description:
Some 16-bit wonders that never were.

A former Sega Technical Institute developer has shared a litany of screenshots, source code, and design documents for various undeveloped and cancelled Sega Mega Drive titles, including an unreleased game starring Sonic the Hedgehog's best buddy, Tails.

In a feature published by gaming curiosity blog The Hidden Palace, former Sega of America employee Ken Rose shared his stories of working within the studio's STI team during the Sega Genesis/Mega Drive's 1990s heyday. Following the interview, Rose then generously shared a selection of floppy discs from his own personal collection, offering a look at several in-development titles that never made it out of the Redwood City offices.

item.title: Nintendo Got the Original Zelda: Ocarina of Time Artist to Draw the Remake's Map
item.description:
"We asked the artist to draw a new map".

Nintendo releases The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 this week, and to drum up (even more) anticipation, the company has released a selection of interviews with the core team behind the shiny new remake (thanks, Nintendo Life).

item.title: Most Triumphant! Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure: Arcade Announced For PC and Consoles
item.description:
SanDimasHighSchoolFootball RULES.

Developer Art of Play has just announced a brand-new arcade adventure based on the iconic 1989 movie Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure. The new game is currently in development for PC and console platforms, with a crowdfunding campaign expected to launch on Backerit in February 2027.

The announcement trailer sees Bill S. Preston, Esq. and Ted "Theodore" Logan revisiting classic scenes from the original film, including their barroom brawl with Billy the Kid, mall mayhem with Napoleon Bonaparte, and a hard-rockin' jam session with Beeth-oven.

item.title: 'What We Do in the Shadows' Gets a Castlevania-Style Homage, and You Can Play It on Your Nintendo DS
item.description:
"We can do nothing but wait".

Regardless of whether you prefer the movie or TV series of What We Do in the Shadows, the simple fact is that it's one of the funniest comic creations of the past few decades – and it now has its own AI-free video game adaptation, even if it's unofficial.

"Laszlovania sets the world of What We Do in the Shadows into an action-adventure like no other," says Edward La Barbera (Frasier Fantasy, Crazy Taxi: Tim Walz Edition), who describes the game as a homage to both "the hit FX show and early Castlevania titles."

item.title: 'It Took a Lot of Work' - the Elusive PS3 Title Like a Dragon: Kenzan! Has Just Received an AI-Free Fan Translation
item.description:
From the same team behind last year's 'Ishin!' patch.

After 18 years, you can now play the jidaigeki-themed Yakuza / Like A Dragon spin-off Like A Dragon: Kenzan! (otherwise known as Ryū ga Gotoku Kenzan!) in English, courtesy of a fan translation.

Released in 2008 for the PS3, Like A Dragon: Kenzan! was released exclusively in Japan, and as such, never got an official English localisation. Unlike the other historical spin-off, Ishin!, It's also never been remade for modern platforms, with the Yakuza executive producer Masayoshi Yokoyama and chief producer Hiroyuki Sakamoto telling the outlet OneMoreGame in 2022 that the reason for remaking Ishin over Kenzan was simply that "many fans wanted an Ishin remake more than Kenzan."
